_comment: Navigation sweep profile for Super Mario Bros. 3 (ADR-0239, F14.16).
Rung used: ADR-0239 s1's second (a published RAM selector pinned for the
run), because no in-game selector reaches another world from power-on.
The game's own selector (rung 1) still does half the work: once the world
is pinned the game loads that world's map, and the entry script walks the
map cursor onto the panel of the world's first level and presses A. The
walk is input, so it is the same kind of pass the Konami code is.
Three game facts this profile had to measure, none of them guessable and
all of them on this checkout's dump (mint-w<N>.txt records each one):
1. $0727 does warp. Pinning it at 0x00-0x07 makes the game load World
1-8's map (verified by screenshot for all eight). The byte in RAM still
reads 00 afterwards - a cheat substitutes the value the CPU reads and
never writes memory - so $0727 itself can NOT be the session's RAM
check: it would read 00 whether the warp happened or not.
2. $070A, the object set, is non-zero inside a level and 0 on the map, so
it is how the entries were found (runs/f1416/smb3/probe/), but it is
not the check either: the blind body CLEARS the level well inside the
120 s budget and the session ends back on the world's map.
3. $0348 reads F1-F8 - the world the game draws in the HUD - and it holds
the same value inside the level and on that world's map, at 15 s and at
120 s. It is the check. It is NOT in the published RAM map: it was found
by diffing the eight worlds' map and level states, and it is a check,
not a cheat, so ADR-0184 s5's 'no code is invented' does not bite - but
it does mean the check is only as good as this measurement.
Read by scripts/record_navigation_sweep.py.

navigation.label: current world - 1
navigation.source: DataCrystal, Super Mario Bros. 3/RAM map (datacrystal.tcrf.net/wiki/Super_Mario_Bros._3/RAM_map): $0727 is "World number - 1", 0x00-0x07 = Worlds 1-8. Published map, cited per ADR-0184 s5. Measured on this dump 2026-09-26: pinning it at the map's load makes the game load that world's map.

_defaultsComment: ADR-0239 s6's budget: 120 emulated seconds, the body repeated to fill the
run as Contra's profile does. The body is this game's only existing stage
route, so the sweep presses the buttons the game's own 1-1 route presses.
What that costs, measured on this dump off each session's rec-final.mss:
the route was authored to CLEAR World 1-1, and worlds 1, 2, 5, 6 and 8
leave or clear their level inside the budget and spend the rest of the run
on that world's map ($070A = 0, $0348 still F1...F8 - no game over), while
worlds 3, 4 and 7 are still in their level at 120 s ($070A = its object
set, the level timer at 100 of 300). The map is new material in its own
right and is recorded deliberately, but the stage-clear transition itself
is not: the selector is pinned for the whole run (ADR-0184's amendment).
The entry scripts are separate mints per world because the map walk
differs per world: the first level's panel is right of the START panel in
Worlds 3 and 4, up in 1, 2 and 5, up-then-right in 6, and down in 7 and 8.
They carry no settle frames between two direction holds - measured, a 40 f
pause moves the panel the A press lands on and Worlds 5 and 6 miss the
level with it and enter without.
_livesComment: No lives pin. ADR-0239 s3 allows one only when a blind body needs it to
stay on the stage, and on this game it does not: four lives are enough.
Measured 2026-09-26, 120 s, the same generated script and the same run for
World 2 and World 8, with `cheat=0736:63` (99 lives, the maximum the
published map gives the counter) and without it: both arms end on the
world's map with $0348 = F2 / F8 and $070A = 0, i.e. the run cleared the
level either way and neither arm reached GAME OVER. The pin also buys no
material: 916 new rule keys against 918 without it on World 2, and 887
against 891 on World 8.
s3's inert control was run anyway, and it FAILS on this game. $0736 is
DataCrystal's "Mario # of Lives", 4 at the start of a game, so the control
is `cheat=0727:00 cheat=0736:04` against `cheat=0727:00`, same generated
script, 120 s: 46 files under textures/ differ (6 written drawn keys, 1891
against 1895; the written tile data is identical), and the final RAM
differs in one byte, $0332 (244 against 243). Two repetitions of each
configuration differ in 0 files, so the difference is the pin's and not the
recorder's replay jitter. s3's sentence "it changes only HUD digits the
game draws anyway" has a counterexample here: within the run the counter
reaches 3 (Mario dies once) while the pin keeps answering 4, and one byte
of game state ends up different. This game therefore could not carry a
lives pin even if a body needed one, and the profile carries none.
_metricComment: ADR-0239 s4's `new` is drawn keys - (tileData, palette) - and it is the
gate; s4 was amended on 2026-09-26 to say so and to exclude the builder's
`defaultTile` placeholders, because on a CHR ROM game the tile-data string
cannot answer s4's question. Measured here: the re-recorded stage-1
baseline names all 8192 CHR indices (0 of 0..8191 missing), so every
session's tile-data set is a subset of it and `newTiles` is 0 for all eight
sessions - the tile-data counts are still reported (tiles 8192 for every
session, seen 561-691, newTiles 0) and s5's reference row is saturated the
same way (8192/8192 = 100% on both sides, and 100% over every rule because
the placeholders enumerate the whole CHR). What moves is the drawn key:
1571 written keys in the baseline against 6972 in the union, and the
reference pack's written drawn keys go from 373/984 (37.9%) to 956/984
(97.2%). The same saturation was measured independently on Excitebike by a
parallel session on the same day. `[every rule: 100.0%]` in the report is a
constant of every bootstrapped pack of this ROM and must never be quoted as
